My personal test for these AIs has been asking it to reason out how to read Thai words. For whatever reason they consistently fail to explain how to read words correctly, hallucinate tone markers, mistake vowels as being tone markers, etc etc.

Okay, tell me the word for “hello” then breakdown how a thai person would go about reading the word in thai script, including all phonetics and how the tone is determined.

I think that the info online for how to read Thai is often incomplete, and AIs struggle to put all the rules together. Could also be that they run out of tokens (idk the technical AI stuff so bear with me) and can’t include the full context of thai language rules in their response, so they end up cutting off their analysis early and hallucinating reasons that the word may have a certain tone, such as adding tone marks that aren’t there.

LLMs do not and cannot know what they know, or know what they don't know, or know about "themselves".  It's inherent in the architecture of LLM models.  Any concept of "self" that it portrays is just a representation of its training data, ie. an "average" response of what it predicts a human (the training data source) would have said if asked the same thing.  In other words, it's physically impossible for an AI model to "look at itself" figuratively speaking, and then draw itself.  It does not have access to view its own weights, or the capability to understand them even if it could.

One of the hallmarks of real AGI will be when that changes - when AIs are actually self-aware, with agency, over their own weights.

Creating pairs of words is not a great way to do translation. There are plenty of words that have multiple pairs, and many words don't have a pair in a target language.
